You are doing a CORRECTNESS code review (read-only — do NOT edit any file). 

CONTEXT: The repo at `C:\Users\olive_\OneDrive\Documentos\codigo\darcy\css-chat-bubble-style\darcy-local` was just transformed into a LOCAL / self-hosted version (Supabase running in Docker via the Supabase CLI, exposed to the internet through a cloudflared/ngrok tunnel) of a sibling project `darcy-nuvem` (which targets cloud Supabase). MOST files are verbatim copies of the already-working nuvem codebase and are OUT OF SCOPE. 

REVIEW ONLY THESE FILES (the ones adapted/authored for the local setup):
1. `supabase/config.toml` — rewritten as a full local Supabase stack config (api/db/studio/auth/storage/edge_runtime + functions + storage bucket seeding).
2. `widget-src/build.mjs` — added a tiny .env loader and esbuild `define` injection of build-time globals.
3. `widget-src/src/services/config.ts` — now consumes esbuild-injected globals `__DARCY_SUPABASE_URL__`, `__DARCY_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY__`, `__DARCY_WIDGET_ASSETS_URL__`, `__DARCY_VOICE_ENABLED__`.
4. `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts` — now reads `import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` with localhost defaults.
5. `src/lib/dashboardApi.ts` — reads `import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL`.
6. `supabase/functions/widget-loader/index.ts` — reads `Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')` to build the Storage fetch URL.

Read each file IN FULL (use Read). Then scrutinize the END-TO-END CHAIN:
- Does the esbuild `define` mechanism actually replace BARE IDENTIFIERS like `__DARCY_VOICE_ENABLED__` (value passed as the string `"true"`/`"false"`) and the `JSON.stringify`'d strings correctly? Is `declare const __DARCY_*__` in config.ts compatible (esbuild does no type-check, but will the identifiers resolve at runtime if a define is missing)?
- `build.mjs` loadDotEnv: parsing correctness (quotes, `=` in values like JWT tokens / URLs with `=`?), precedence vs process.env, and whether it loads `../.env` relative to build.mjs correctly.
- `config.ts` `API_VOICE_WS`: `SUPABASE_URL.replace(/^http/, 'ws')` — correct for `https://`→`wss://` and `http://`→`ws://`? Any edge case?
- `config.toml`: is every key VALID for a recent Supabase CLI (v2.101)? Flag any key that could be renamed/removed/misplaced and would make `supabase start` ERROR OUT. Specifically scrutinize: `[storage.buckets.ativos]` and `[storage.buckets.widget-assets]` (is a hyphen in the bucket table key valid? is `objects_path` the correct field name?), `[edge_runtime] policy="oneshot"`, `[auth] enable_signup`, `[auth.email] enable_signup`, `[db] major_version=17`, `[db.pooler]`. 
- `widget-loader/index.ts`: is `SUPABASE_URL` actually injected into local edge functions by the Supabase runtime? Does the public Storage path it builds work locally?
- The hardcoded default anon key string — is it the correct standard Supabase local-dev anon JWT?

Report UP TO 8 candidate findings. For each: `file`, `line`, one-line `summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario` (what input/state → what breaks). Be recall-biased: surface anything a careful reviewer would flag, including config keys you are not 100% sure are valid for the CLI version. Return them as a JSON array. Keep total response under 600 words.

- prd: Generate a Product Requirements Document (PRD) for a new feature. Use when planning a feature, starting a new project, or when asked to create a PRD. Triggers on: create a prd, write prd for, plan this feature, requirements for, spec out.
- ralph: Convert PRDs to prd.json format for the Ralph autonomous agent system. Use when you have an existing PRD and need to convert it to Ralph's JSON format. Triggers on: convert this prd, turn this into ralph format, create prd.json from this, ralph json.
- recap-do-dia: Lê tudo que foi feito hoje (sessões Claude Code, commits git, tasks Todoist) e gera o mix certo de conteúdo pra X — short posts diários + thread candidata pro banco semanal — escrevendo no Notion para copy-paste manual.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	// Config do widget. LOCAL/self-hosted: os valores abaixo são INJETADOS em build time
2	// pelo esbuild (widget-src/build.mjs) a partir das envs do .env da raiz (darcy-local/.env):
3	//   SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, WIDGET_ASSETS_URL, VOICE_ENABLED.
4	// Defaults (quando a env não está setada) = Supabase LOCAL em http://127.0.0.1:54321.
5	//
6	// IMPORTANTE (produção tunelada): o widget roda no NAVEGADOR do aluno dentro do Moodle,
7	// então SUPABASE_URL precisa ser a URL PÚBLICA do túnel (cloudflared/ngrok que expõe a
8	// porta 54321/kong), NÃO 127.0.0.1. Rode o build com SUPABASE_URL=https://<seu-tunnel>
9	// e re-semeie o bucket `ativos` (ver README-LOCAL.md / build-widget script).
10	declare const __DARCY_SUPABASE_URL__: string;
11	declare const __DARCY_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY__: string;
12	declare const __DARCY_WIDGET_ASSETS_URL__: string;
13	declare const __DARCY_VOICE_ENABLED__: boolean;

16	const SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = __DARCY_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY__;
17	// http(s) -> ws(s) para o proxy de voz (WebSocket).
18	const WS_BASE = SUPABASE_URL.replace(/^http/, 'ws');
19	
20	export const CONFIG = {
21	    SUPABASE_URL,
22	    SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
23	    WIDGET_ASSETS_URL: __DARCY_WIDGET_ASSETS_URL__,
24	    API_CHAT: `${SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/darcy-chat`,
25	    API_ANALYTICS: `${SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/analytics`,
26	    // WebSocket proxy para conversação voz-a-voz (xAI Realtime via darcy-voice edge function)
27	    API_VOICE_WS: `${WS_BASE}/functions/v1/darcy-voice`,
28	    // Feature flag — VOZ LIGADA PARA TESTE (2026-05-26). Requer XAI_API_KEY setado
29	    // no secret da edge function darcy-voice (senão retorna 500 "XAI_API_KEY not set").
30	    // PENDENTE antes de alunos reais (motivos pelos quais estava off):
31	    // (1) consentimento LGPD explícito antes do getUserMedia,
32	    // (2) rate limit por usuário/dia (custo xAI Realtime).
33	    VOICE_ENABLED: __DARCY_VOICE_ENABLED__,
34	};
